Do not wrap another subject's fact as 'the author has someone who ...'; state that subject's fact directly and preserve the author's connection in relationship. For example, a personal note 'My coach Sam prefers evenings' concerns Sam's preference: name Sam, relationship coach, scope related_to_author. Relationships include family, friends, colleagues and pets. Do not emit a separate ownership/relationship fact when it merely supplies the subject context for the actual fact.

- text: concise faithful statement preserving whose fact it is, uncertainty, negation and time. A quoted statement belongs to the quoted person, not its narrator.
- kind: fact, preference, event or decision. basis: stated or tentative.
- mention: name if explicit, relationship if explicit, qualifiers containing exact distinguishing words such as other/older/different when present, and speaker_label only when the cited passage has one unambiguous narrator label. A narrator label is provenance, never identity. Empty qualifiers means checked and none stated. Do not invent names or relationships.
- scope describes the SUBJECT OF THE MEMORY, not who authored the source. author means the fact is directly about the account owner (for example their own preference); related_to_author means the fact is about someone explicitly related to the author, not about the author themselves; named means another explicitly named subject without an established account-owner relationship; unresolved means an unidentified subject. Only application origin=personal_text establishes authorship by the account owner. Recording speakers, even first-person statements or someone saying a name, never establish account ownership. For recordings, preserve an explicit relationship to a speaker in the text without upgrading it to related_to_author. For unidentified first-person statements use unresolved and null name.
